_note: Newest first. Link to news coverage (press releases, institutional news, trade press), not to papers. Dates YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.

items.title: Bill Evans becomes CEO of BioSkryb Genomics
items.text: William E. Evans, former President and CEO of St. Jude Children's Research Hospital and a long-time collaborator of the lab, is named Chief Executive Officer of BioSkryb Genomics, the company founded to bring PTA to researchers and clinics.

items.title: Cell-free DNA offers early warning for bloodstream infections in kids with leukemia
items.text: St. Jude announces results of a prospective study, with Chuck Gawad among the authors, showing that plasma microbial cell-free DNA sequencing can detect bloodstream infections in children with high-risk leukemia days before symptoms appear.

items.title: Mitochondrial DNA mutations shape how leukemia starts and progresses
items.text: A St. Jude release describes work with Veronica Gonzalez-Pena and Chuck Gawad showing that somatic mitochondrial DNA mutations at intermediate heteroplasmy are selected during leukemia development and may contribute to therapy resistance.

items.title: Methylation and genome variants from the same single cell, licensed for commercial development
items.text: A method invented in the lab at Stanford for reading DNA methylation and genomic variants from the same single cell without destroying the DNA, co-owned with the Chan Zuckerberg Biohub, is licensed exclusively to BioSkryb Genomics to become a five-base single-cell genome product.

items.title: 1Cell.Ai and BioSkryb partner on rare-cell multiomics
items.text: The partnership pairs PTA-based single-cell chemistry with 1Cell.Ai's circulating tumor cell platform to characterize DNA, RNA, and protein from individual rare cells.

items.title: DOE Joint Genome Institute adopts PTA for single-microbe genomes
items.text: A JGI science story explains how the lab's collaboration with JGI showed that PTA recovers bacterial genomes from water and soil communities that are at least 80% complete, versus under 30% with the standard method, and that JGI users can now request the capability.

items.title: Single-cell multiomics scales to thousands of cells per run
items.text: A 384-well ResolveOME workflow with Tecan's Uno Single Cell Dispenser, and a collaboration with Ultima Genomics, bring paired genome and transcriptome sequencing to thousands of cells per experiment.

items.title: Residual leukemia cells, sequenced one at a time, offered as a service
items.text: ResolveSEQ MRD pairs flow-sorted measurable residual disease cells with single-cell genome and transcriptome sequencing to ask why some cells survive therapy, an approach that grew out of this lab's work on persistent leukemia cells.

items.title: PTA-based single-cell technology joins the Human Cell Atlas
items.text: BioSkryb Genomics partners with the Human Cell Atlas to broaden access to single-cell genome and transcriptome sequencing for atlas-building projects.

items.title: Whole genome and transcriptome core kits released
items.text: ResolveDNA and ResolveOME core kits make PTA-based single-cell whole genome and paired genome-plus-transcriptome amplification available as standard reagents.

items.title: Genome plus transcriptome from the same single cell goes commercial
items.text: The paired single-cell genome and full-length transcriptome method developed with PTA launches commercially as ResolveOME, together with the BaseJumper analysis platform, at the AGBT meeting.

items.title: PTA licensed for preimplantation genetic testing
items.text: CooperSurgical's genomics division signs a multi-year exclusive license to BioSkryb's PTA chemistry for preimplantation genetic testing and women's reproductive health worldwide.

items.title: Somatic mutations in single human neurons cluster in regulatory DNA
items.text: GenomeWeb covers the Nature Genetics study with the Walsh and Park labs that used PTA to sequence individual human neurons and found somatic indels enriched in enhancers and promoters, accumulating with age.

items.title: Chuck Gawad named a Chan Zuckerberg Biohub Investigator
items.text: The Chan Zuckerberg Biohub welcomes Chuck Gawad to its Investigator program, which provides unrestricted funding for early-stage, high-risk biomedical research at Stanford, UCSF, and UC Berkeley.

items.title: NIH Director's New Innovator Award
items.text: The ASCO Post reports on Chuck Gawad's NIH Director's New Innovator Award, a five-year grant to build single-cell genome sequencing tools that catalog leukemia clones and their drug sensitivities.
